turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Hi Lucy Beck, Jordan Lee from Eleno. Thanks for making time to talk about Craftwork. We build custom AI agents and workflow automation for growing businesses, and a fixed-scope build usually lands between $25,000 and $45,000, with a short paid discovery phase in front of it.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Hi Jordan. I should say upfront that we're eight people in Northcote, some of them casual. We sell craft supplies and run weekend workshops. That number is more than we spend on rent in a quarter.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Understood, and we do scale the scope. The smallest thing we build for a retailer like yours is usually a booking and enquiry agent that answers workshop questions, holds places and pushes the confirmed bookings into your systems without anyone retyping them.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: My daughter built us a booking spreadsheet that does most of this. It's not elegant, but it works and it costs nothing.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Spreadsheets are fine until the volume moves. Once you're running four workshops a week, the enquiries, the waitlists and the refunds all land in one inbox, and that inbox is you. Automation takes the repetitive part off the owner.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: The inbox is me, that's true. But it's maybe twenty emails a week, and I quite like knowing who's coming.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: That familiarity is worth keeping, and an agent doesn't remove it. What it removes is the retyping, the double bookings and the late replies. We deploy it into your own systems and transfer the intellectual property to you, so there's no ongoing subscription.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Transferring the ownership sounds good, but I'd still be paying for the build, and the build is the part I can't cover.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: There's a managed optimisation option afterwards as well, from about $1,500 a month, which keeps the agent tuned as your workshop mix changes. Most clients see the payback inside six months once the hours come back.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Six months of payback assumes those hours are worth something in cash. For us they're just my evenings.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Your evenings are the cost. Owners undervalue that constantly. If we take five hours a week back, that's two hundred and fifty hours a year, and it's the difference between opening a second shop and staying where you are.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: We're not opening a second shop. We're trying to make this one pay for itself.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Then the case is stronger, because margin in retail comes from the parts nobody wants to do. Stock reordering, supplier emails, workshop reminders, the follow-up note that sells the next class. All of that is automatable.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Some of that I actually enjoy. The follow-up notes are how people come back.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I will send a one-page overview of the build packages so you can see what is included at each level. It sets out the discovery phase, the fixed build and what the handover looks like.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Send it, but please don't put me on a call schedule. I know the answer for this year.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Fair. Although I'd say the businesses that wait usually wait until something breaks. A missed workshop, a supplier order that never went out, a refund that sat for three weeks. That's when the phone call happens, and it's more expensive then.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Nothing has broken in four years.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Nothing had broken for the last retailer I spoke to either, right up until their stock system stopped talking to their online store during a sale weekend. The point of building this now is that you choose the timing.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Or the point of waiting is that I spend the money on stock instead.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Both can be true. What I'd encourage is looking at the annual number rather than the project number. Spread across three years with the ownership in your hands, a build that removes five hours a week is cheap per hour.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: I don't think in per-hour terms. I think in whether the bank balance survives February.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: That's exactly why the discovery phase exists. It's short, it's fixed, and it tells you what is worth automating before you commit to a build. Plenty of clients stop after discovery with a plan and no build.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: A plan I can't afford to act on isn't much use to me.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: It's a plan you can act on in stages. Start with the booking agent, add the supplier reordering next year, then the reporting. We build in fixed scopes precisely so it doesn't have to be one big commitment.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Staged still starts at the first stage, and the first stage is the part I'm saying no to.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Understood. I'll keep the overview practical rather than glossy, with the inclusions, the assumptions and an honest note on where this sort of automation doesn't pay for a team your size.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: That last part would be the useful bit, honestly.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Then I'll lead with it. And if the workshop side grows, or you take on wholesale, the numbers change quickly and it's worth another look.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Lucy Beck
turns.text: Thanks Jordan. Good luck with it, but we'll stay as we are.
